docs.text: Start Here Welcome to the Heartlands Codex, the lore and reference hub for the Heartlands series. The core of the series is exploration, with a focus on making the world feel like a living place that reacts to its history, cultures, and people. Series Overview The Heartlands series is currently in development with three titles: * Heartlands: The Arena * Heartlands: The Lost Colony * Heartlands Timeline All games take place in the Second Era of the world. Relative to the events of Heartlands : * Heartlands: The Arena takes place about 15 years before. * Heartlands: The Lost Colony takes place about 50 years before. Canon Policy Everything in this Codex and in the games is canon unless explicitly labeled otherwise. docs.text: Endurance Endurance is how much damage you can sustain, and how fast you recover from injury. Endurance governs the skills of Marksman , [Health], Block , Heavy Armor , Repair , Unarmored

docs.text: Intelligence Intelligence is the measure of your mind. It determines the size of your magic pool and your mastery of [Magic]. Intelligence governs the skills of Alchemy , Enchanting , Herbology , and Wand .

docs.text: Ashenhorn These towering, nightmarish humanoid beasts have gaunt frames, leathery ash-brown skin, and elongated claws that give them a feral, almost demonic presence. A jagged obsidian horn juts from its head, framing a snarling maw filled with jagged teeth. A ragged mane of coarse hair runs along its back, accentuating its savage silhouette. Crude armor, shackles, and chains cling to its limbs, hinting that it was once bound — or perhaps unleashed — from captivity. Known in dark legends as a relentless hunter, the Ashenhorn is feared not only for its brutal strength and speed, but for the way it stalks its prey with crude intelligence.

docs.text: Bat Bats are winged denizens of the night, their membranous wings stretch over elongated, claw tipped fingers. Their eyes gleam in the moonlight with eerie intelligence, their high pitched cries rippling through the darkness. They navigate the blackest caves and midnight skies, through ecoholocation, sensing the world in ways no mortal eye can see. While many feast on swarming insects or the sweet nectar of night blooming flowers, darker breeds thirst for blood, descending in silent swarms to drain their prey. Described in folklore as the harbingers of curses and companions to witches or vampires, bats are a symbol of dread as they are creatures of the natural world

docs.text: Bear Brown Bear: Hulking lords of the forest, their massive forms cloaked in thick, earth-colored fur that ripples with muscles beneath. Though often solitary and deliberate in their movements, a brown bears charge is a thunderous explosionm of power. With claws as long as a mans hand and a roar that can shake leaves from the trees, they command respect and fear from all who wander their domain. Some legends tell of bears so ancient and wise that moss grows along their backs and their eyes burn with the golden fire of the sun. Grizzly Bear: Fearsome titans of the wild, their hulking frames draped in thick fur that bristles like a the pelt of a storm cloud. Standing on their hind legs, they tower over most creatures, eyes glinting with primal, unwavering resolve. Each swipe of their massive claws can shatter bone, with their thunderous roars echoing through valleys like the call of an anciet guardian. Some say the greatest of them bear silver scars from battles with frost giants, and their spirits roam the wilds long after their bodies have returned to earth.

docs.text: Birds Birds are the swift and watchful wanderers of the skies, from small, seed-spreading songbirds to sharp-eyed raptors. Seen as divine messengers in many cultures, they can be gentle or fiercely territorial, defending nests with beak and claw. In battle, trained hawks and falcons strike with precision, using speed and surprise to disorient their foes.

docs.text: Boar Boars are stocky, muscle‑bound beasts with coarse bristled hides and tusks sharp enough to pierce armor. Known for their stubborn resilience and explosive charges, they are feared both in the wild and in the arena, where their sheer strength can topple even seasoned fighters. Wild boars are fiercely territorial, defending their herds with relentless fury, while trained war‑boars are prized mounts and shock‑troop beasts. Among the most famous is Bacon, a loyal companion boar whose iron will and battle‑hardened tusks have saved many a warrior from certain defeat.

Among the most famous is Bacon, a loyal companion boar whose iron will and battle‑hardened tusks have saved many a warrior from certain defeat.

docs.text: Camel Camels are the stalwart ships of the desert, their long legs and padded feet carrying them effortlessly across shifting dunes. Their humps hold precious reserves, allowing them to endure searing heat, biting cold, and long stretches without water. Calm and deliberate by nature, they are loyal to those who treat them well, yet quick to spit, bite, or kick when provoked. In the arena, war‑camels are towering, intimidating mounts, their steady gait and unshakable endurance making them as dangerous in prolonged battles as they are in sudden, crushing charges.

Their keen senses and quick reflexes make them natural predators, capable of striking with lightning speed when threatened. In many cultures, cats are seen as omens. Among the more well‑known felines is Paul, the soot‑dusted companion of Maergrim the undercroft blacksmith, often found curled atop the forge or watching customers with a knowing, unblinking stare.

docs.text: Cave Troll Cave Trolls are hulking, dim‑witted brutes that dwell in the deepest caverns and shadowed mountain passes. Their thick, stone‑gray hides are as tough as granite, shrugging off all but the heaviest blows, while their immense strength allows them to crush boulders and bones with ease. Though slow of thought, they are relentless once roused to anger, pursuing prey with single‑minded fury. Many wield crude clubs made from fallen timbers or jagged rock, using them to devastating effect in both ambushes and open combat. Legends claim that some cave trolls can heal from almost any wound, their bodies knitting back together so long as they remain in darkness.

Rare white stags are said to be messengers of the gods, appearing only to those destined for great journeys.

Wherever they march, the ground is left scorched and cracked, as if the fires of the underworld had clawed their way to the surface.

docs.text: Driada Driada are mystical guardians of the forest, their forms a graceful blend of woman and tree. Their skin bears the texture and hue of living bark, while hair like cascading leaves shifts with the seasons—lush green in summer, fiery red in autumn, and bare branches in winter’s rest. They move with the stillness of deep woods, yet strike with the swiftness of wind through the canopy, wielding vines, roots, and thorned branches as living weapons. Driada are deeply bound to their chosen grove, drawing strength from the soil beneath them and the ancient trees around them. Corrupted Driada are forest guardians twisted by blight, shadow magic, or the lingering touch of death. Their once‑lush foliage withers to blackened thorns, and their bark‑like skin splits to reveal oozing sap the color of dried blood. Where they walk, grass shrivels and roots curl away, and their whispers carry promises of despair. No longer protectors, these beings lure intruders deeper into the woods, only to ensnare them in vines that drain life until nothing remains but husk and bone.

docs.text: Fish Fish fill rivers, lakes, and coastal waters with flickers of silver, gold, and every hue between. Fishermen prize them for their meat, shimmering scales, and in rare cases, magical properties such as the moon‑scaled trout said to glow faintly at night, or the golden riverfish believed to bring prosperity to whoever catches it.

docs.text: Fungoid Fungoids are eerie, humanoid mushroom‑creatures that thrive in the damp gloom of caves, swamps, and deep forests. Their bodies are a blend of sinewy muscle and fibrous mycelium, with caps and spore‑laden growths sprouting from their heads and limbs. Moving with slow, unsettling precision, they fight with both physical strength and the toxic weaponry of their fungal nature, releasing choking clouds of spores that blind, poison, or ensnare their prey. Some are known to plant their victims in the soil, allowing creeping roots to overtake the body until nothing remains but another Fungoid. Though often solitary, larger colonies act as a single, hive‑minded organism, defending their territory with unwavering persistence.

docs.text: Gloomfang Gloomfangs are twisted, predatory creatures born of shadow and bone. Their elongated, sinewy frames are topped with a natural, horned skull structure, fused seamlessly to their flesh as both head and armor. Jagged bone ridges frame their pale, glimmering eyes, while their namesake fangs, long, curved, and black‑tipped, jut from a snarling maw built to tear through hide and armor alike. Coarse, dark fur bristles along their spine, standing on end when they ready to strike. docs.text: Harpy Harpies are vicious, winged predators with the body of a bird of prey and the upper form of a twisted, wild‑eyed woman. Their talons are razor‑sharp, capable of rending flesh in an instant, while their long, feathered wings carry them in swift, diving strikes from above. Harpies hunt in flocks, using ear‑piercing screeches to disorient prey before dragging it into the air or tearing it apart on the ground. They are drawn to high cliffs and jagged peaks, where their nests of bones and feathers overlook the lands they terrorize. In dark folklore, harpies are said to be cursed spirits of the envious, doomed to hunger eternally for the lives they can never reclaim.

docs.text: Hellhound Hellhounds are fearsome, infernal beasts wreathed in the stench of brimstone, their eyes glowing with a malevolent red light. Their dark, sinewy hides are marred with bone‑like spines jutting from their backs, and their snarling maws reveal fangs that burn with unnatural heat. Born of the lower planes, hellhounds are relentless hunters, able to track prey by scent across any terrain, and even through the veil between worlds. Their bite can sear flesh, while their guttural growls echo like distant thunder. Legends claim they are the chosen hounds of didren lords, loosed to punish oathbreakers and drag the damned into the fires below. Fire Resistance: 25% Weakness to Shock: 20%

docs.text: Horse Horses are swift, powerful steeds valued for their speed, endurance, and loyalty. From sturdy workhorses pulling heavy loads to sleek chargers thundering across battlefields, they have long been trusted companions to travelers, farmers, and warriors alike. Their keen instincts and strong bonds with their riders make them dependable in both calm and chaos, carrying their masters through treacherous terrain or straight into the heart of danger. In some cultures, certain horses are believed to be touched by magic, able to sense approaching storms, find safe paths in the wild, or ride tirelessly for days without rest.

docs.text: Mimic Door Mimics are devious shapeshifters that disguise themselves as ordinary doors, patiently waiting for an unsuspecting victim to approach. The moment a hand reaches for the handle, the mimic’s surface splits into a gaping maw lined with jagged teeth, and adhesive tendrils lash out to ensnare prey. Their wooden‑like hides can perfectly imitate aged oak, polished mahogany, or even rusted iron, making them almost impossible to spot until it’s too late. Book Mimics lure the curious by taking the form of ancient tomes, often adorned with ornate bindings or strange runes. When opened, the “pages” unfold into snapping jaws and grasping tongue‑like appendages, eager to pull the reader in. Some secrete a paralytic ink, rendering prey helpless while the mimic feeds. Scholars whisper of rare, intelligent Book Mimics that can speak and use their disguise to tempt victims with forbidden knowledge before devouring them.

docs.text: Moon Shadow Moonshadows are elusive, otherworldly hunters cloaked in darkness and silver light. Their sleek forms seem to blur at the edges, as if part of them exists just beyond the mortal realm. Under moonlight, their eyes gleam like pale orbs, and their movements become almost impossibly fast, striking and vanishing before prey can react. Moonshadows are silent stalkers, able to slip through cracks, melt into shadows, and pass unseen even in open spaces. Folklore claims they are born from the union of night spirits and lunar magic, and that those who see one in its true form are fated to dream of it until the day it comes to claim them.

docs.text: Mushroom Guy Redcap Clubbers are stout, round‑bodied mushroom folk with bright crimson caps flecked with pale spots. Though small in stature, they are surprisingly strong, wielding heavy stone clubs with a clumsy yet brutal swing. Their thick, spongy bodies absorb blows, and their earthy scent can mask them perfectly among forest undergrowth. Redcap Clubbers are territorial and quick to anger, often gathering in small bands to drive intruders from their fungal groves. Sporefang Creepers are hunched, menacing mushroom creatures with mottled brown caps that conceal clusters of needle‑like fungal spines. Their gnarled limbs end in sharp claws, used to grip prey while releasing clouds of toxic spores. They prefer to lie in wait, camouflaged among rotting logs and leaf litter, before ambushing anything that wanders too close. Wounds from their claws can quickly fester as invasive mycelium begins to take root in the victim’s flesh.

docs.text: Octopus Octopuses are intelligent, elusive predators of the deep, their soft, boneless bodies allowing them to squeeze through the narrowest cracks and crevices. With eight agile arms lined with powerful suckers, they can grasp, manipulate, and ensnare prey with precision. Masters of disguise, they shift their skin’s color and texture to blend seamlessly into coral, rock, or sand, striking with sudden bursts of speed. In maritime lore, octopuses are seen as tricksters and escape artists, slipping away from nets and cages as if by magic. Some sailors tell of giant octopuses large enough to drag a man, or an entire skiff into the depths without a sound.

docs.text: Pig Pigs are sturdy, resourceful livestock kept for their meat, hides, and remarkable ability to forage almost anywhere. With sharp noses and an unending appetite, they root through soil for roots, fungi, and scraps, thriving in both farmyards and the wild. Though often docile, a threatened or cornered pig can bite fiercely and charge with surprising strength. In rural folklore, pigs are symbols of abundance and good fortune, while some tales warn of enchanted boars that began life as ordinary swine.

docs.text: Plant Monster Bloomstalkers are carnivorous plant beasts that lure prey with the vibrant, jewel‑like buds and flowers coiled around their tall, twisting stalks. Their broad leaves hide thorned tendrils capable of lashing out with whip‑like speed, pulling victims toward the plant’s central, sealed bud, where rows of hidden, petal‑lined teeth wait to consume them whole. The twisting vine body is strong enough to crush bone, and its surface glistens with a faint, sweet‑smelling sap that masks the creature’s true danger. Bloomstalkers thrive in humid jungles and enchanted groves, often rooted near water sources to ambush creatures that come to drink.

docs.text: Quagth Quagths are squat, amphibious predators with wide, tooth‑filled maws and bulbous, unblinking eyes that gleam like molten gold. Their thick, mottled blue‑green skin helps them blend into swamps and jungle undergrowth, while small curling vines sprout from their backs, masking their presence until they strike. Despite their rounded bodies, Quagths are deceptively fast, lurching forward in sudden bursts to clamp down on prey with crushing force. Known for their unsettling, gurgling laughter, they are as much ambush hunters as they are scavengers, dragging their catch into murky water to drown it before feeding.

docs.text: Rabbit Rabbits are quick‑footed, soft‑furred herbivores found in meadows, forests, and farmlands. With their keen hearing and powerful hind legs, they can vanish into the underbrush in the blink of an eye. Though gentle by nature, rabbits are resourceful survivors, creating intricate burrow networks to evade predators. In folklore, they are symbols of luck, fertility, and cleverness, sometimes said to be messengers of forest spirits or shapeshifters in disguise.

docs.text: Rat Rats are small, quick, and highly adaptable scavengers found in cities, sewers, forests, and farmlands alike. Their sharp teeth and relentless appetites drive them to gnaw through wood, rope, and even thin metal in search of food. Living in large colonies, rats can quickly overrun an area, spreading disease and spoiling supplies. While often dismissed as pests, their cunning, survival instincts, and sheer numbers make them a persistent threat, especially when hunger drives them to swarm.

Their piercing eyes and forked tongues constantly taste the air, allowing them to track prey with uncanny precision. In ancient myths, Serpens are often depicted as guardians of hidden treasures or sacred places, their patience matched only by their lethality.

The chains, half-buried in their fibrous flesh, drag along the ground with a constant metallic rattle, serving both as restraints and as weapons, whipping outward to ensnare prey before hauling it into the creature’s waiting mouth.

docs.text: Skeletons Skeletons are the reanimated remains of the dead, bound to unholy magic or cursed duty. Their empty eye sockets glow with pale, unnatural light, and their brittle bones move with eerie precision. Skeleton Archers are the undead marksman that weild ancient, splintered bows and quivers of black-fletched arrows. Skeleton Footmen however are armed with dented shields and rusted blades. They march in grim formations, their clattering bones echoing across the battlefield. Skeleton Gentlemen, better known as Gents, retain fragments of their former refinement. Dressed in decayed finery, they wield elegant walking sticks with surprising precision. Skeleton Sorcerers channel the dark magic that animates them, hurling necrotic blasts, summoning fresh undead from the bones of the fallen. Skeleton Warlords are massive and heavily armored, commanding lesser undead with guttural human roars. Skeleton Knights, clad in corroded plate and mounted upon equally undead steeds, thunder into battle with lance and sword.

docs.text: Twig People Skinny Twigkin are wiry, brittle‑limbed forest sprites made from gnarled twigs and bark. Their spindly frames allow them to slip through undergrowth unseen, striking with thorny claws or small, sharpened sticks. They often act as scouts and skirmishers, harassing intruders before vanishing into the trees. Their bodies creak and snap as they move, the sound often mistaken for nothing more than wind in the branches, until it’s too late. Round Twigkin are squat, knotted creatures resembling bundles of brambles and roots. Their thicker frames make them sturdier than their slender kin, capable of bashing foes with heavy, club‑like limbs. They tend to serve as defenders for Twigkin groves, standing their ground while the skinnier ones dart in and out to harry enemies. When still, they can easily be mistaken for a simple heap of forest debris, springing to life only when prey wanders too close.

docs.text: Wraith Wraiths are malevolent spirits consumed by rage and hunger, their skeletal forms wrapped in shadow‑stained robes that seem to drink in the light around them. Their bones are darkened by centuries of corruption, and their clawed fingers are long enough to pierce both armor and soul. Unlike lesser ghosts, wraiths possess cunning and malice, stalking their prey with deliberate patience before striking. Their presence bleeds the warmth from the air, and their chilling laughter can shatter the resolve of even seasoned warriors. Legends claim a wraith’s touch can strip away fragments of a victim’s spirit, leaving behind only a hollow shell fated to join their spectral ranks.

docs.text: Alchemist's Guild Guild's Philosophy: The Alchemists Guild is dedicated to the study and mastery of alchemy; it was created long ago by an alchemist in the search of a master elixir that would grant him immortality, it is unknown if he succeeded. Their goals include discovering new potions, ingredients, transmutation of materials, and history of alchemy. Location: The guild is situated in the Old District, where they have access to a variety of ingredients from the market and can sell their potions to a diverse clientele. The guildhall could be a mix of a mystical apothecary and a scholarly research institute, filled with bubbling potions, ancient books, mysterious artifacts, and rare ingredients that can only be obtained at higher ranks. Novice Mixer: Discovery Quest: Learn about and gather basic ingredients in the local area. Potion Requirement: Craft a Basic Detection Potion to find hidden ingredients. Apprentice Alchemist: Discovery Quest: Research a recently discovered herb and its properties. Potion Requirement: Brew a Potion to help decipher ancient texts about the herb. Potion Brewer: Discovery Quest: Investigate a series of potion failures and find the cause. Potion Requirement: Craft a series of potions correctly. Herbalist: Discovery Quest: Locate and study a rare and elusive plant species. Potion Requirement: Create a one time potion to communicate with plant life to find a rare ingredient. (We could possible create a magic effect for the player where plants near them would glow as a reward) Elixir Crafter: Discovery Quest: Help another guild member with their research in combining certain ingredients and reporting the results. Potion Requirement: Craft the potion the guild member is researching. Gain the ability to craft 2 potions for the price of 1 Transmuter: Discovery Quest: Uncover the secrets of an ancient transmutation formula while on a dungeon expedition for more ingredients. Potion Requirement: Brew a Potion to make you basically hallucinate the location (dungeon) of a hidden formula for transmutation at alchemical benches, unlocking this ability. (This should be easy to adapt into our potion system) Master Alchemist: Discovery Quest: Restore a lost alchemical recipe from fragmented manuscripts. Potion Requirement: Create a Potion to recall and piece together the recipe. Gain the ability to make 3 potions for the price of 1 Alchemical Scholar: Discovery Quest: Delve into the history of alchemy and uncover forgotten techniques through several dungeons. Potion Requirement: Craft a Potion to interpret old alchemical symbols. Elixir Virtuoso: Discovery Quest: Discover the formula for a legendary elixir thought to be mythical. Potion Requirement: Unlock the final components of the elixir using transmutation. Grandmaster Alchemist: Discovery Quest: Lead a groundbreaking project to create a groundbreaking alchemical substance. Potion Requirement: Develop a Master Alchemist's Elixir. (This would be a crazy good potion that had very long and powerful effects, to be determined) Additional Quests: Research and Exploration: Quests that require the player to explore new locations, gather rare ingredients, and research ancient alchemical lore. Interactions with the mages guild. Guild Contribution: Beyond potion crafting, players contribute to the guild by expanding its library and collection of rare ingredients.

docs.text: Blackwater Brotherhood Guild Overview Focuses on piracy, smuggling, and seafaring raiding. Opposes the Mariners' Guild, disrupting trade routes, and engaging in illegal activities at sea and in the Harbor District. Guild Ranks Deck Hand: Quest: "Smuggler's Initiation": Prove your worth by successfully smuggling a small shipment of contraband goods from the Harbor District into the old district, evading the Mariners' Guild patrols. Sea Rogue: Quest: "The Silent Raid": Participate in a stealthy raid on a coastal warehouse, stealing supplies and valuables for the Brotherhood. Corsair: Quest: "The Merchant's Folly": Ambush and plunder a merchant ship, using intelligence gathered by the Thieves Guild to avoid heavily guarded routes. Saboteur: Quest: "Undermining the Sentinels": Sabotage the Mariners' Guild operations by planting false information and disabling their ships covertly at night. Treasure Hunter: Quest: "Secrets of the Deep": Locate and retrieve a treasure, rumored to be cursed, using a map acquired by the Thieves Guild. Pirate Captain: Quest: "The Fortress Assault": Lead an assault on a rival pirate stronghold to establish the Brotherhood's dominance.

docs.text: Mages Guild Guild Ranks and quests Mage Initiate: Quest: Find a tome containing a basic illumination spell and use it to navigate a dark, enchanted library to find a book. Apprentice Mage: Quest: Retrieve a tome with a minor shield spell to protect yourself from a magical creature. Journeyman Mage: Quest: Cast a fire rune to deal with the guardians in a dungeon library. Spellweaver: Quest: Apply an illusion spell to infiltrate and gather intelligence from a meeting of rogue spellcasters. Arcanist: Quest: Use conjuration to protect a sacred site from being desecrated by roguemages. Expert Mage: Quest : Investigate and close a dangerous rift inadvertently opened by a rogue mage. Magical Scholar: Quest: Discover an ancient tome detailing the history of magic in the world, providing insights to resolve a series of magical anomalies that the rogue mages have caused. Master Mage: Quest: Use a powerful dispelling spell to dismantle a network of dark magic corrupting key figures in the city. Archmage: Quest: Retrieve a tome that will teach you a spell to help you uncover the identity of who is in charge of the rogue mages. Guild Master: Quest: Use every school of magic to defeat a group of rogue mages. Additional Quests: Political Intrigue: Navigate the politics within the guild and the broader world, as the use and control of magic can have significant societal impacts. Inter-Guild Dynamics: Interactions with other guilds like the Alchemists and Thieves Guilds, either in cooperation or conflict, based on the various magical interests and the impact of magic on their operations. Magical Artifact Recovery: Locate and retrieve powerful magical artifacts that have been stolen by the rogue mages. The quest would involve tracking down the thieves, overcoming magical traps, and safely securing the artifact. Magical Duel Tournaments: Participate in tournaments against other mages. This could be a series of duels that test different aspects of magical prowess, like precision, spell combination, and knowledge of the schools of magic..

docs.text: Thieves Guild Guild's Origin and Philosophy: “The Shadow Hands”(Placeholder name) were founded by a charismatic figure known as "The First Shadow." This individual was born poor but through luck and hard work climbed the ladder to become wealthy he was then wronged by the city's elite and saw the suffering of the poor that they helped cause firsthand. The guild operates on principles akin to Robin Hood, stealing from the corrupt wealthy to aid the downtrodden. However, they are careful to maintain their mythic status to avoid direct confrontation with the city's powers. Guild Ranks: Novice Thief: Initial rank upon joining. Initiation Quest: Prove your worth by completing a simple theft in the Old District. Training Missions: Learn basic thieving skills like lockpicking and sneaking. Apprentice Thief: Mentor Assignment: Assigned a mentor from higher ranks. Advanced Theft Quests: Execute more complex thefts under mentor guidance. Skilled Thief: Starts to build a reputation, gaining more challenging tasks. Solo Operations: Begin undertaking solo missions after the death of your mentor. Skill Demonstration: A quest to showcase advanced thieving abilities. Master Thief: Heist Planning: Start planning and executing significant heists. Resource Management: Tasked with managing loot and assets from heists. Shadow Agent: Espionage Quests: Gather intelligence on wealthy targets and corrupt officials. Inter-Guild Diplomacy: Act as a liaison with other underground factions. Guild Envoy: Alliance Missions: Forge alliances with other organizations. Negotiation Quests: Engage in high-stakes negotiations on behalf of the guild. Wealth Distributor: In charge of redistributing wealth among the poor. Manages resources and ensures the guild’s ethos is upheld. Keeper of Secrets: Guild Lore Quests: Uncover and protect the secrets and history of the guild. Advisor Role: Offer strategic advice for guild operations. Second Shadow: Leadership Quests: Make crucial decisions in the absence of the Guild Master who has been arrested.. Attempt to free the guild master. First Shadow: Ultimate Heist: A grand, final heist that the original guildmaster never got to finish, solidifies the player's position as the leader. Guild Management: Oversee all guild operations and make pivotal decisions. Additional Quests: Introduction to the Guild: Catching Rumors/Getting Caught: The PC either overhears rumors about the guild in taverns or gets caught stealing, leading to an encounter with a guild member. Rising Through the Ranks: The Robin Hood Acts: Multiple quests involve stealing from the rich in innovative ways (like infiltrating a lavish party) and helping to distribute wealth or goods to the poor in the Poor District. Uncovering Plots: Quests that involve gathering intelligence on plots by the wealthy to exploit the poor, leading to missions to sabotage these plans. Unraveling Corruption: Guard's Corruption: Tasks to expose corrupt guards, involving stealth and gathering incriminating evidence. Infiltration Mission: Infiltrating the town guard or gaining the trust of higher-up guards to learn about corrupt officials and their dealings with the city's elite. Aid the Poor: Randomly generated quests to help individual poor families or individuals. Dungeon Crawls: Retrieving rare items from dangerous locations outside the city. Integration with the Larger Game World: Impact on the City: The guild's actions should visibly affect the city, like improved conditions in the Poor District, or changes in NPC behavior and dialogue.

docs.text: Combat Basics Combat in Heartlands is tactile and physical. Weapons have weight and momentum, so solid swings matter more than light taps. You will need to hit with intent or the weapon may bounce instead of dealing damage. Two-Handed Weapons Some weapons are designed to be used with two hands. They hit harder and can also be used to block, functioning like a shield in a pinch. Larger blades and heavy weapons are the usual candidates for two-handed use. Shields And Shield Bash Shields are more than defense. If an enemy gets close, you can shield bash to deal damage and possibly knock them over, creating an opening. Shield size matters for both protection and bash impact. See Shield Types for details. Resistances And Weaknesses Enemies can have resistances and weaknesses to certain damage types. For example, some enemies resist fire but are weak to frost. Pay attention and adjust your loadout accordingly. Looting Fallen Enemies To loot a fallen opponent, grab their body and an inventory shelf will rise above them. You can then take whatever you want.

docs.text: Combat in Heartlands is tactile and physical. Weapons have weight and momentum, so solid swings matter more than light taps. You will need to hit with intent or the weapon may bounce instead of dealing damage.
docs.title: Combat Basics

docs.text: Some weapons are designed to be used with two hands. They hit harder and can also be used to block, functioning like a shield in a pinch. Larger blades and heavy weapons are the usual candidates for two-handed use.
docs.title: Two-Handed Weapons

docs.text: Shields are more than defense. If an enemy gets close, you can shield bash to deal damage and possibly knock them over, creating an opening. Shield size matters for both protection and bash impact. See Shield Types for details.
docs.title: Shields And Shield Bash

docs.text: Enemies can have resistances and weaknesses to certain damage types. For example, some enemies resist fire but are weak to frost. Pay attention and adjust your loadout accordingly.
docs.title: Resistances And Weaknesses

docs.text: Equipment And Holsters Holsters You have several holsters on your body: one on each hip, one on each shoulder, and one on the small of your back for shields. To store a weapon, place it near the holster until you feel a vibration, then release. To retrieve it, grab near the holster location. Quivers When you equip a bow, your best arrows are automatically placed into a quiver on your back or hip (based on your settings). When you grab an arrow, an outline shows you where to nock it. Equipping Armor Open the Armor category, grab a piece, and move it to the appropriate body slot (Head, Chest, Hands, Legs, Feet). To remove armor, grab it off the mannequin. Weapon Charge And Repair When a weapon runs out of charge, it returns to your inventory. Recharge it by holding a Heart Shard in one hand and the depleted weapon in the other, then hold the trigger on the hand with the Heart Shard until it is destroyed. If a weapon breaks, it returns to your inventory. Repair weapons and armor at repair stations in the world.

docs.text: Shield Types Shields can be used for more than just defense. If an enemy gets close, you can shield bash them to deal a bit of damage and possibly knock them over, giving you a chance to strike. Buckler Shields Buckler shields are small and light. They offer modest protection but are fast to use and stay out of the way. A buckler bash can stagger an enemy, but it won’t hit as hard as larger shields. Standard Shields Standard shields are a balanced choice. They provide solid protection and can deal noticeable damage when you bash. They are large enough to matter in a fight without slowing you down too much. Great Shields Great shields are large and towering. They offer the best protection but are heavy and can make it harder to see. A bash from a great shield is powerful and will almost certainly put an enemy on the ground.

docs.text: Spell Casting There are many kinds of spells in Heartlands: spells that deal damage, spells that prevent harm, spells that summon allies, and spells that influence the minds of others. Beyond what a spell does, each spell also has a casting style. Understanding these casting styles will help you choose the right spell for the situation. Projectile Spells Projectile spells launch a bolt or ball of magic toward a target. They are great for direct damage at range, and their effectiveness depends on your aim, distance, and line of sight. Fireballs and frostbolts are classic examples. Placement Spells Placement spells are aimed at a location rather than a target. They have a maximum placement distance and always land where you are looking. Placement spells include several subtypes: Rune Spells : Place a magical trap that triggers when an enemy approaches. Ground Spells : Create an effect on the ground that harms or hinders enemies within a radius. Sky Spells : Call magic down from above to strike an area. Placement spells are ideal for area control, ambushes, and setting up fights on your terms. Channel Spells Channel spells project a continuous stream of magic, more like a magical flamethrower than a single cast. They are best used when you can keep pressure on a target, but they also require you to stay exposed while channeling. Self Spells Self spells are cast on yourself by throwing the spell upward. They are typically used for recovery or protection, such as healing health or curing poison.

docs.text: Alchemy System The alchemy system operates using an alchemy bench, which players must locate in the game world. Alchemy benches are designed to be clearly labeled and easily recognizable. They typically feature a green glow around the bench itself and an adjacent sign displaying a potion icon. It was suggested that a picture of an alchemy bench should be included in the documentation for clarity. The alchemy bench interface is divided into several sections. On the right side of the bench, players will find a list of all their available ingredients. Players can grab ingredients from this shelf and place them into the cauldron situated in front of them. The cauldron is capable of holding a maximum of three ingredients at one time. As ingredients are added to the cauldron, they will be seen floating in jars behind it, with information detailing each of their effects. To successfully create a potion, there must be at least more than one of the combined ingredients that contains the same effect. The strength of the resulting potion is directly determined by the player's current level in the alchemy skill. To complete the crafting process and create the potion, the player must grab the bellows located beneath the cauldron and move them up and down three times to stoke the fire. If a potion is successfully created, it will spawn directly above the cauldron and rotate until the player grabs it. Once obtained, the player has the option to drink the potion immediately or add it to their inventory. If the ingredients added to the cauldron do not produce any usable effects, the crafting process will result in a "failed potion."
docs.title: Alchemy System

docs.text: Health Health is determined by endurance and level. It is the amount of damage you can withstand. It does not regenerate automatically. In order to regeneratre your health you must sleep, use food, potions or spells.
docs.title: Health

docs.text: Health is determined by endurance and level. It is the amount of damage you can withstand. It does not regenerate automatically. In order to regeneratre your health you must sleep, use food, potions or spells.
docs.title: Health

docs.text: Magic Magic is required to cast spells. Its max value is determined by intelligence. It regenerates automatically based on your willpower.
docs.title: Magic

docs.text: Magic is required to cast spells. Its max value is determined by intelligence. It regenerates automatically based on your willpower.

docs.text: Before the Gods...
docs.title: Primordials

docs.text: The Primordials Before the Gods: Before gods, before mortals, before worlds—there existed the Primordials. These were not gods nor beings, but raw cosmic principles, pure forces of reality itself. Their presence was so immense and alien that naming them with mortal tongues bordered on futility. Yet mortals, ever curious, named the first and greatest of these forces Oris, the embodiment of pure existence, endlessly wandering the infinite Void. In its solitary eternity, Oris grew lonely and began to fracture. From these fractures arose two sentient entities: Vaoris and Eloris. With their birth, Oris faded back into the Void itself, leaving the two beings alone. Vaoris, embodying change and chaos, yearned for transformation, progression, and expression. Eloris, embodying order and stability, desired permanence, structure, and tranquility. Their clashes sparked new ideas, consciousness, and entities, filling the void around them with complex constructs and ethereal thoughts. Eventually, their struggles gave rise to countless sentient forms known as The Dren, beings of pure thought without physical shape. Seeking coherence, Vaoris and Eloris constructed a new realm called Oravyn, a sanctuary distinct from the Void, forcing the Dren into tangible forms. Having fulfilled their roles, Vaoris and Eloris withdrew silently into the Void, leaving Oravyn to its new inhabitants. Initially furious at their entrapment, the Dren erupted into endless conflict, tearing each other apart only to recombine endlessly due to their immortality. Their existence became marked by eternal cycles of destruction and rebirth. After eons of pointless war, a realization struck the Dren: their only escape from physical form lay in constructing new realms within Oravyn and pouring their essence into these creations, shedding physicality entirely. Divided by differing visions, the Dren split into two factions: the Didren and the Adren. The Didren pursued individualistic visions, creating countless separate realms collectively known as Mythara, each reflecting their personal desires, ambitions, and vanity. In contrast, the Adren unified their efforts into one grand realm called Erasyl, populating it with mortal life to house their essences and provide a harmonious existence. The Didren, envious of the Adren's collective achievement, repeatedly assaulted Erasyl, but the Adren defended and rebuilt tirelessly. At a crucial turning point, the Adren discovered how to strip immortality away when a powerful Didren named Orathis attacked Erasyl. They succeeded in killing him, scattering his essence throughout Oravyn, the largest chunk becoming the moon Thirel. This act created pure magical energy and Heart Shards—fragments capable of containing and focusing this newfound magic. Large fragments known as Heart Stones, extremely powerful and dangerous, fell to Erasyl, altering reality itself and even causing new continents to rise around them. Alarmed and enraged, the Didren captured an Adren named Gammis, determined to learn this secret of destruction. Under immense torment, Gammis eventually relented, revealing the method. The Didren tested it on him, confirming its devastating effectiveness. Realizing their newfound vulnerability, both factions spiraled into catastrophic warfare, their battles shattering realms and scattering fragments of their essence across Oravyn. Eventually, desperate and dwindling, the Adren executed a final, costly strategy. They sacrificed most of themselves to imprison the Didren within their own realms of Mythara, creating eternal prisons from their very essences. Although successful, this left only a handful of weakened Adren surviving, unable to physically shape Erasyl but able to subtly influence its fate through whispers, visions, and subtle manipulations. These surviving Adren became the first true gods worshiped by mortals, embodying virtues and ideals essential to mortal life and civilization: Maldara: Goddess of affection, unity, friendship, marriage, and emotional bonds. Jalar: God of ingenuity, builders, tools, and skilled labor; brother of Jaral. Jaral: Keeper of knowledge, logic, insight, reason, and scholarly wisdom; brother of Jalar. Orelian: God of trade, wealth, prosperity, and negotiation. Sylador: Overseer of fate, history, and the passage of time. Seren: Patron of creativity, inspiration, performers, artists, and poets. Mahar: God of worldly pleasures, indulgence, luxury, and celebration. Vaelia: Goddess of the heavens, winds, seas, natural harmony, weather, and tranquility. Kaelos: God of charity, generosity, luck, fortune, travelers, and goodwill. Valdaris: God of justice, peace, law, and moral order. The imprisoned Didren became deities of darker domains, each sealed within their realms, forever plotting to break free and reclaim their lost power: Kaerith: Cruelty, torture, pain, and vengeance. Nykareth: Tricks, greed, deception, thieves, and cunning plots. Xalrok: Chaos, destruction, ruin, and disorder. Xalrik: Strict, oppressive order; absolute discipline and ruthless conformity. Malicyn: Curses, malice, hexes, and dark magic. Morvala: Murder, brutality, bloodshed, and mortal agony. Jakora: Seduction, infidelity, betrayal, temptation, and corruption. Zhaedria: Darkness, shadows, fear, nightmares, secrecy, and hidden evil. Pestaris: Disease, pestilence, decay, illness, and corruption. Gammorath: Madness, insanity, delusion, mental torment, and chaos. Thus began the universe of Heartlands, shaped by the eternal echoes of these cosmic struggles, forever marked by the interplay between the remnants of Adren benevolence and the imprisoned malice of the Didren. Mortals, unknowingly inheriting the echoes of this great conflict, live in a world forever touched by magic, divine intervention, and the lingering threat of ancient, imprisoned powers yearning for freedom. Though trapped, the Didren send mortal servants into Erasyl to spread chaos, undermining stability and attempting to break free.

Malicyn: Curses, malice, hexes, and dark magic. Morvala: Murder, brutality, bloodshed, and mortal agony. Jakora: Seduction, infidelity, betrayal, temptation, and corruption. Zhaedria: Darkness, shadows, fear, nightmares, secrecy, and hidden evil. Pestaris: Disease, pestilence, decay, illness, and corruption. Gammorath: Madness, insanity, delusion, mental torment, and chaos. Thus began the universe of Heartlands, shaped by the eternal echoes of these cosmic struggles, forever marked by the interplay between the remnants of Adren benevolence and the imprisoned malice of the Didren. Mortals, unknowingly inheriting the echoes of this great conflict, live in a world forever touched by magic, divine intervention, and the lingering threat of ancient, imprisoned powers yearning for freedom. Though trapped, the Didren send mortal servants into Erasyl to spread chaos, undermining stability and attempting to break free.

docs.text: Nature and Function of Heart Shards Heart Shards are not mere magical batteries. They are crystallized echoes of divine emotion (love, wrath, hope, despair), layered into complex resonant matrices. Each Heart Shard pulses with the intent of its origin, and no two are precisely alike. Uses Small shards might enhance spells, hold enchantments, or act as arcane keys. Heart Stones can warp reality around them, anchor divine miracles, or even alter the passage of time in localized pockets.

docs.text: Origin of Heart Shards The Shattering of Divinity When Oris, the First, fractured into Vaoris and Eloris, their clash birthed not just time and form, but the tension between them. This divine conflict culminated in the Mythic Wars, where the Adren and Didren, once thoughtforms known as the Dren, embodied themselves and waged battle across the planes. See The Primordials and Gods . In the final cataclysm of that war, when the Adren sacrificed much of their essence to seal the Didren into Mythara, shards of their divine will and emotion were cast into the mortal plane. These became Heart Shards: fragments of thought, feeling, and raw purpose, solidified by the intensity of that final sacrifice. Some claim Thirel, the third moon, is the greatest of these: the broken heart of an Adren who gave their very soul to seal the rift between realms.

docs.text: Binding The Storm Hecdor would become. He was effective, but cruel: often those facing Hecdor would take much longer to recover from their wounds than any other combatant. He was powerful, but arrogance is no substitute for humility: though it was his talent and skill that saw his success there was no acknowledgement of all those who had helped him achieve his goals. He saw those in the arena only as opponents or tools, never friends. As time continued to march ever forward, it seemed that Hecdor slipped ever backwards. It was far too late to stop the momentum of his descent by the time anyone realized the truth of what occurred. A young man, who lived a life destitute and dull, now found himself surrounded by wealth and power the likes of which he could never have dreamed. He took a new name for himself: Stormbinder. This was the title he fought under for so long. The title that turned a boy into a monster. None who were there will ever forget the horror of his final match. The match that made him arena master. he had been cultivating for many years, and it was ready to bloom. Hecdor fought with a fury that would shake even the core of the gods. When the prior master lay broken at Hecdor's feet, pleading for their life, Hecdor announced the dawn of the blight that has plagued our arena for many years: the blood price. No longer would arena matches be for show, no longer would we spar for exhibition, now was the time of matches fought to the death. The former master was the first who paid this evil tax, and more have followed since. The arena has fallen to the abyss that many others have: the pursuit of wealth at the expense of morals. Lore Book

docs.text: Invisible Pain Do you ever look for danger? Are you anxious day and night? Probably not if you’re normal and have adapted to your surroundings. I, however, am always anxious and seeking out danger. My brain is always searching for something to be wrong, even when things are great. You could call it a learned behavior of the mind. Why would anyone do this to themselves? It is not by choice, it is inherently engrained since childhood. Such fear and anxiousness also cause physical manifestations. Some say you are cursed by Kaerith, but it has not yet been proven. Oh yes, constant head pain and back pain can plague you from this condition. Due to these manifestations, I have decided to seek out the Saloen monks. I have heard tales of them being great healers in the empire, and perhaps they can help someone like me. This book marks the beginning of my journey to ending this invisible pain and suffering. Lore Book

docs.text: Lithoponics A Study ...Though the process of growing flora in controlled environments has been practiced for longer than any person can remember there have been few agricultural advancements as significant as the field of lithoponics. A relatively new field of science, brought on by the discovery of vitalite crystals, lithoponics has led to many unique aspects of agriculture that were previously considered fantasy. First, let us examine some of the unique properties of the catalyst of lithoponics: the vitalite. Vitalite was discovered somewhat by accident. A party of adventurers was descending into what they believed was a recently revealed dungeon. I shan't go into specifics here, but suffice to say they found a large room of thriving plant life previously believed to only be capable of growing on the surface. This room was illuminated by a number of strange crystals, and after some communication with members of the scientific community and some more expeditions, these crystals were officially discovered and given the name vitalite. The most remarkable aspect of these fascinating crystals is one that scientists and arcanists alike are still baffled by: vitalite emits pulses of blue to UV light frequencies. What this means is that vitalite has the ability to function as a light source for small scale agricultural applications. The frequencies of light that are emitted prompt root and leaf growth (making it very good at aiding the growth of various herbs) and the slow pulses of light emitted give enough intermittent activity to simulate a "night cycle" for the plants. Although these traits of vitalite prove incredibly useful and will likely continue to be researched, vitalite is unable to be used in any large scale capacity. As of this writing vitalite cannot be artificially grown, making the procurement of crystals expensive, and it takes many of the crystals to produce viable crops. However, as previously mentioned, vitalite can be used in small scale lithoponics operations where rapidly growing, small scale plants are required. Perhaps the most well executed example of lithoponics exists within the Rustfall arena. The arena staff were able to convert a portion of their infirmary to a small lithoponics wing, enabling certain crucial ingredients to be grown in house. We shall see if in time, the capabilities of such facilities can be developed, and if lithoponics will become a staple of the modern age... Lore Book

The arena staff were able to convert a portion of their infirmary to a small lithoponics wing, enabling certain crucial ingredients to be grown in house. We shall see if in time, the capabilities of such facilities can be developed, and if lithoponics will become a staple of the modern age... Lore Book

docs.text: The Vigil People of Rustfall, our world is under siege yet again, this time by the so-called "innovative" field of lithoponics. Let me tell you, this isn't innovation-it's a ticking time bomb. At the heart of this controversy is the vitalite crystals: mystical rocks touted for their ability to emit radiation that makes plants grow. But before we blindly bow down to these "Life Stones" let's take a look at this catastrophe we're welcoming with open arms. First and foremost, we don't have any studies on long term effects of vitalite. We're being asked to trust that these crystals are safe, but where's the proof? What are the long-term impacts of vitalite radiation on plants? I 'd like to see whatever mutant squash these so-called scientists grew, but we've gotten nothing! We've seen this narrative before-introduce a new technology, say it's going to revolutionize its field, and when it inevitably goes wrong, the public -you, me, us- pays the price. What do humans and elves look like 10 years down the road of eating these plants? We need answers, not blind faith. While we're looking at food production, let's not forget the backbone of our food supply: traditional, family oriented farmers. Farmers like my good friend Vonrath. Lithoponics threatens to disrupt centuries-old agricultural practices, like Vonrath's combined 10 generations of experience between him and his family. Imagine how this will affect these hard working farmers and their ability to provide fresh, quality produce and choice cuts of meat to the various markets and restaurants of the greater Rustfall area. This isn't just about new technology-it's about sidelining an entire community that has built up the backbone of society for centuries! We have to stand firm against the reckless adoption of vitalite in farming. We demand comprehensive, long term studies to understand the true impact of lithoponics-because above all, we must prioritize the health and safety of our communities. Don't let yourself be fooled by the glimmer of vitalite. We must stand strong against this threat to our future, our health, our way of life. Don't allow yourself to lose all this for the sake of progress. Lore Book

docs.text: The Origins of Magical Healing The practice of magical healing has been present for as long as the written word. Yet, how has this practice come to be? If we are to believe those more pious than I - who claim the gods have set in motion our perpetual ignorance to keep us from matching their power - why then are we permitted to mend our wounds beyond our natural medicine? Why then may we reverse the progression of illnesses, regrow lost limbs, and even put a stopper on death? Various healing magics are practiced widely by every culture across the Empire. Yet there is no concensus as to why we are able to heal this way. Saloen monks believe healing comes from channeling abnormal energies caused by sickness or wounds. Various Kadian theologians believe magical healing is an emulation of their own divine heritage, a gift to those born beneath the influence of the gods. Even the various human cultures of the empire have different shamanistic beliefs around the act of healing, often mixing natural healing with chants and rites to invoke spirits. Despite these beliefs, there is no clear answer on how healing came about. While it is usually not a good practice to utilize powers not fully understood, we can assume the generations before us whose of healing has come without significant issues are good enough indications for their continued use. Restoration Skill Book

docs.text: Ex The Chosens Path ...I trudged unto the place of healing, my axe splintered and my shield crushed to my arm. This was the place for those broken by battle. As Hanndri, who is the great healer of my people, stripped me of my armor and lowered me into those waters of eternal steam and salt... I felt myself change. Those pains suffered from a lost battle were washed away. The shame of loss flowed from my mind. No longer was I a warrior who suffered defeat. I was but a man. A man who suffered pain. And as the wounds of my body began to mend under Hanndri's chants, my thoughts eased and my resolve renewed. I rose from those waters changed: no longer enduring the pain of my injuries, but bearing the wisdom they carried with them. Block Skill Book

docs.text: Executioner's Journal 16 Eththo, 212 Today was the first of what I'm sure will be many executions. I thought it would be easy. It always looked so easy when I watched the executioner as a kid. But the cabbages I trained on didn't prepare me for a real beheading. The sickening feedback through the axe as I hit this poor bastard's spine... It felt like snapping a thick parsnip. As my blade carried through his neck, I was reminded why we wear the mask. The thick veins that carry blood to the man's brain released their pressure and coated me in his hot blood. All these sensations hit me at once, and the smell of iron assaulted my nose... I choked my morning's meal back down, and began to clean the blade. Short Blades Skill Book

docs.text: Stabs From Afar At first glance, this book simply contains drawings of standard attacks and guards that are used while wielding a longsword. Upon further examination, you discover this is a very raunchy romance novel, with the diagrams acting as double entendre and various metaphors for the main characters' sexual exploits. You get the sense this book was likely passed around by initiates of some religious order, whose belongings are regularly searched. This was likely a way for them to trade means of indulgence without detection from their superiors. Long Blades Skill Book

docs.text: African Violets Saintpaulia is a section within Streptocarpus subgenus Streptocarpella, consisting of about ten species of herbaceous, perennial flowering plants in the family Gesneriaceae. They are native to Tanzania and adjacent areas of southeastern Kenya in eastern tropical Africa. Delicate, velevet-petaled blooms that shimmer with a faint silvery sheen under moonlight. Alchemists prize the flowers for their subtle yet potent magic- when steeped into an elixir, they are ground into a fine violet powder and added to dream draughts, guiding the sleeper into visions of peace and clarity. Folklore warns, that blooms plucked without care will wither instantly, losing their power; only those harvested while humming softly to the plant will retain their full potency. docs.text: Allium Globe shaped clusters of starry blooms that emit a sharp, pungnet aroma. They are beloved by healters, their roots and bulbs hold a biting essence that wards against corruption, curses, and the touch of the undead. Crushed fresh allium releases a potent oil used in protective wards, barrier salves, and truth serums that compel honesty. In ancient grimoires, it is said that silver petaled allium blooms only bloom under a blood moon and can be brewed into an elixir that reveals hidden lies or banishes shadow-dwelling creatures. While common forms grow in sunlit fields and kitchen gardens, wild mountain allium is far more dangerous to harvest- its sharp scent draws hungry nightbeasts that feed on its rare magic vitality. docs.text: Anemone Delicate, cup-shaped blooms that sway in the gentle breeze, as if whispering secrets to the wind. Their petals, which can range from snowy white to deep crimson, are said to close in sorrow on days of mourning and open wide under the first rays of dawn. Alchemists value anemones for their connections to the fleeting nature of life- they are often steeped into potions of protection, renewal and safe passage through dangerous journeys. In folklore, white anemones are offered to soothe restless spirits, while red varieties often hold the power to ward off misfortune and betrayal. The rare midnight anemone, with petals the color of a moonless sky, is rumored to grant visions of the past and future when brewed into a starlight infused draught. docs.text: Apple Apples are among the most storied fruits in herbal lore. Their crisp flesh and sweet fragrance hide a wealth of magical potential. Red Apples, shaded as warmly as the autumn sun, are prized for vitality tonics and love elixirs. Passion and love are stirred, strengthening the bond between companions. Green Apples, tart and sharp are used in brews that sharpen the senses. They often fortify courage and can dispel most illusions. Golden skinned apples are imbued with the magic of sunlight- when distilled into a potion, they can restore strength to te weary, heal greivous wounds, or extend life itself. Brown rotten apples, though shunned by common folk, are treasured by necromancers and shadow-sorcerers; their decaying flesh holds the essence of entropy, lending power to curses, blight spells, and potions that drain vitality. Alchemists warn: An apple plucked under a new moon may carry a hidden curse, twisting its magic into something more perilous. Item stats Item stats Weight 0.0 Value 0.0 Armor 0.0

Herbalists speak of parsley as a “restoring leaf,” one that coaxes sluggish vitality back into motion and sweeps away lingering weariness like a cool wind over the fields. docs.text: Ichpo Atu (The Smiling Islands) The Smiling Islands Capital: Israluna Dominant Race: Antanians Landscape: Lush tropical islands, coral bays, volcanic islets Essence Scattered like laughter upon the ocean’s breath, the Smiling Islands are a realm of song, spirit, and mystery. The Antanians, catlike and clever, navigate their archipelago with sail and sense, ruled more by consensus than crown. Here, the boundaries between mortal and spirit blur; festivals last for moons, and the wind itself carries omens. Though distant from the imperial throne, their mastery of sea‑trade and spirit‑binding is unmatched.

docs.text: Irgavorn (The Spine of Storms) The Spine of Storms Capital: Korundal Dominant Race: Saloens Landscape: Jagged mountains, alpine tundra, ancient pine forests Essence Carved from stone and silence, Irgavorn is a realm of peaks and echoes, where the Saloens speak little but mean much. Stoic and enduring, their mountainholds are lined with runes of binding, their forges echo with the wisdom of stone. It is said the winds of Irgavorn still carry the voices of the Adren, for the silence here is deep enough to hold divine memory. Irgavorn guards the north and its secrets with granite will.

docs.text: Khurvann (Khurvak) The Bleeding North Capital: Dravosk Dominant Race: Usai Landscape: Taiga, glacial rivers, frost‑covered steppe Essence Stark and brutal, Khurvann remembers a thousand scars. Home to the Usai, the wolf‑blooded, it is a land forged in war and ice. Here, clan loyalties are blood‑bound, and the old songs are sung in growls and roars. They speak often of the Great Silence—a mythic hush before the world’s end. Yet for all their violence, the Usai hold deep honor. When they fight, they fight as storm incarnate. When they swear fealty, it is eternal.

docs.text: Tazareth (The Shifting Edge) The Shifting Edge Capital: Tazhul Dominant Race: Rocca Landscape: Coastal deserts, salt flats, montane forests Essence Heat and hunger shaped the Rocca, and so too does Tazareth—sun‑drenched and defiant. Its people build into cliff and dune, mastering the harsh winds and scarce water with tenacity. Here, salt is wealth, and water is life’s ransom. The Rocca’s famed Sandcallers commune with spirits of wind and fire, shaping glass and flame into weapons and song. Tazareth breeds survivors and seekers—many a famed imperial explorer hails from these dust‑ridden coasts.

docs.text: Valenmark (Kadia) The Crown of Empire Capital: Caelthor Dominant Race: Kadians Landscape: Rolling grasslands, temperate forests, fertile river valleys Essence The heart and helm of the Velassian Empire, Valenmark is the seat of Emperor Andurion Velasi, whose lineage stretches back to the Unification Wars. It is a land of marble cities and golden halls, where Heart Shards gleam in arcane towers and the bureaucracy of empire churns with tireless precision. The Kadians are statesmen and warriors, philosophers and tacticians, rulers by destiny, not merely decree.

docs.text: Virellia (The Blossoming Expanse) The Blossoming Expanse Capital: Virella Dominant Race: Terrans Landscape: Subtropical forests, waterfalls, tree savannas Essence In Virellia, life spills over with abundance. Terran cities perch in the boughs of titanic trees, their streets a dance of birdsong and flowerlight. Their culture reveres balance and renewal, drawing from ancient symbiosis with nature. Artisans, dreamers, and alchemists flourish beneath the green canopy, often guided by druidic circles and Heart Shard groves. To live in Virellia is to live with the forest, not merely within it.

docs.text: Zircara (The Verdant Shroud) The Verdant Shroud Capital: Ziranu Dominant Race: Nymaa Landscape: Tropical rainforests, mangrove swamps, mist‑drenched deltas Essence Zircara is a realm half‑seen—draped in mist and myth, its secrets guarded by shadow and vine. The Nymaa, serpentkin of sharp wit and ritual grace, rule with a silent elegance. Alchemy, espionage, and the subtle arts flourish beneath the canopy. It is whispered that in Zircara, old gods yet slumber beneath the roots, and the jungle itself decides who lives and who vanishes. Outsiders often find themselves watched… and rarely welcomed.

docs.text: Gods The gods of Heartlands are divided into two great courts: the Adren, stewards of light and balance, and the Didren, forces of shadow and discord. Both shape the world in profound ways. The Adren (Gods of Light, Balance, and Benevolence) They are the stewards of harmony, shepherds of mortal hope. Though their presence is often subtle, their influence binds the Empire in faith and purpose. Maldara, Heartbinder Goddess of affection, unity, and emotional bonds. Her temples host marriages and peace treaties alike. It is said her breath is the wind that softens blades of war. Jalar, Forgefather God of engineering, invention, and physical labor. His hammer shapes not just tools and machines, but civilization itself. Brother of Jaral. Jaral, The Silent Watcher God of wisdom and reason. Cold and calculating, yet never cruel, he guards the great libraries and minds of Erasyl. Scholars call on him with ink and silence. Brother of Jalar. Orelian, Coinbearer God of commerce and prosperity. Ships that sail under his blessing seldom falter. His followers believe that wealth, properly earned, is divine tribute. Sylador, Chronarch God of time and fate. He sees all roads yet walks none. His followers are oracles and timekeepers. Seren, The First Song God of art, music, and dreams. Every masterpiece is a hymn to Seren; every bard, a vessel of his divine melody. Mahar, Mistress of Revels Goddess of pleasure, indulgence, and celebration. To her faithful, joy is a sacred rite. Her festivals light the night skies of Valenmark in fire and fragrance. Vaelia, Skywarden Goddess of nature, weather, and tranquility. Her dominion is the living world, each leaf and stormcloud. In Zircara, jungle priests invoke her name before each monsoon. Kaelos, Luckwhisper God of fortune and travel. A trickster of good humor and divine chance, he aids gamblers, wanderers, and those who take bold steps into the unknown. Valdaris, Judgestar God of law, peace, and justice. His scales weigh kings and commoners alike. His clerics often serve as magistrates throughout the Velassian Empire. The Didren (Gods of Shadow, Discord, and Malevolence) They are the corrosive truth behind all fear. Where the Adren build, the Didren unravel. Not evil in the mortal sense, but forces of entropy, hunger, and raw power. Kaerith, The Flayer God of cruelty, suffering, and punishment. His domain is the scream that follows silence. Worshiped in secret by torturers and warlords. Realm: Korvaeth — a Mythara realm of eternal cruelty and endless torment. Nykareth, Hollow Tongue God of trickery, greed, and lies. He whispers into contracts and promises, turning them sour. His presence is always felt where trust dies. Realm: Velikar — a Mythara realm of deception, greed, and hidden traps. Xalrok, Worldbreaker God of chaos and destruction. Every volcano and riot bears his breath. In the Chaos Era, it was said he walked freely, sowing ruin for sport. Realm: Xarokai — a Mythara realm of chaos, ruin, and perpetual upheaval. Xalrik, The Iron Rule God of oppressive order. docs.text: The gods of Heartlands are divided into two great courts: the Adren, stewards of light and balance, and the Didren, forces of shadow and discord. Both shape the world in profound ways.
docs.title: Gods

docs.text: They are the stewards of harmony, shepherds of mortal hope. Though their presence is often subtle, their influence binds the Empire in faith and purpose.
docs.title: The Adren (Gods of Light, Balance, and Benevolence)

docs.text: Goddess of affection, unity, and emotional bonds. Her temples host marriages and peace treaties alike. It is said her breath is the wind that softens blades of war.
docs.title: Maldara, Heartbinder

docs.text: God of engineering, invention, and physical labor. His hammer shapes not just tools and machines, but civilization itself. Brother of Jaral.
docs.title: Jalar, Forgefather

docs.text: God of wisdom and reason. Cold and calculating, yet never cruel, he guards the great libraries and minds of Erasyl. Scholars call on him with ink and silence. Brother of Jalar.
docs.title: Jaral, The Silent Watcher

docs.text: God of commerce and prosperity. Ships that sail under his blessing seldom falter. His followers believe that wealth, properly earned, is divine tribute.
docs.title: Orelian, Coinbearer

docs.text: God of time and fate. He sees all roads yet walks none. His followers are oracles and timekeepers.
docs.title: Sylador, Chronarch

docs.text: God of art, music, and dreams. Every masterpiece is a hymn to Seren; every bard, a vessel of his divine melody.
docs.title: Seren, The First Song

docs.text: Goddess of pleasure, indulgence, and celebration. To her faithful, joy is a sacred rite. Her festivals light the night skies of Valenmark in fire and fragrance.
docs.title: Mahar, Mistress of Revels

docs.text: Goddess of nature, weather, and tranquility. Her dominion is the living world, each leaf and stormcloud. In Zircara, jungle priests invoke her name before each monsoon.
docs.title: Vaelia, Skywarden

docs.text: God of fortune and travel. A trickster of good humor and divine chance, he aids gamblers, wanderers, and those who take bold steps into the unknown.
docs.title: Kaelos, Luckwhisper

docs.text: God of law, peace, and justice. His scales weigh kings and commoners alike. His clerics often serve as magistrates throughout the Velassian Empire.
docs.title: Valdaris, Judgestar

docs.text: They are the corrosive truth behind all fear. Where the Adren build, the Didren unravel. Not evil in the mortal sense, but forces of entropy, hunger, and raw power.
docs.title: The Didren (Gods of Shadow, Discord, and Malevolence)

docs.text: God of cruelty, suffering, and punishment. His domain is the scream that follows silence. Worshiped in secret by torturers and warlords. Realm: Korvaeth — a Mythara realm of eternal cruelty and endless torment.
docs.title: Kaerith, The Flayer

docs.text: God of trickery, greed, and lies. He whispers into contracts and promises, turning them sour. His presence is always felt where trust dies. Realm: Velikar — a Mythara realm of deception, greed, and hidden traps.

docs.text: The Primordials Before gods, before mortals, before worlds, there existed the Primordials: raw cosmic principles, pure forces of reality. Mortal names barely contain them, but the first and greatest is remembered as Oris, the embodiment of pure existence wandering the infinite Void. Oris, Vaoris, and Eloris In its solitary eternity, Oris began to fracture. From those fractures arose two sentient entities: Vaoris and Eloris. With their birth, Oris faded back into the Void, leaving the two beings alone. Vaoris embodies change and chaos, yearning for transformation and expression. Eloris embodies order and stability, seeking permanence and structure. Their clashes sparked new ideas, consciousness, and entities, filling the void with complex constructs and ethereal thoughts. The Dren and Oravyn Their struggles gave rise to countless sentient forms known as the Dren, beings of pure thought without physical shape. Seeking coherence, Vaoris and Eloris constructed a new realm called Oravyn and forced the Dren into tangible forms. Having fulfilled their roles, Vaoris and Eloris withdrew silently into the Void, leaving Oravyn to its inhabitants. Initially furious at their entrapment, the Dren erupted into endless conflict, tearing each other apart only to recombine due to their immortality. After eons of war, a realization took hold: escape from physical form required building new realms within Oravyn and pouring their essence into those creations. The Adren and the Didren The Dren split into two factions. The Didren pursued individual visions, creating countless realms known as Mythara, each reflecting their personal desires and vanity. The Adren united their efforts to create a single grand realm, Erasyl, and populated it with mortal life to house their essences in harmony. The Didren, envious of the Adren’s achievement, repeatedly assaulted Erasyl. The Adren defended and rebuilt tirelessly. The Death of Orathis and the Heart Shards At a turning point, the Adren discovered how to strip immortality away when a powerful Didren named Orathis attacked Erasyl. They succeeded in killing him, scattering his essence throughout Oravyn. The largest fragment became the moon Thirel. This act birthed pure magical energy and Heart Shards: fragments capable of containing and focusing this new magic. Large fragments, known as Heart Stones, fell to Erasyl, warping reality and even raising new continents around them. See also: Heart Shards

docs.text: Kadian Emperor Quick Jump Background Personality Related Characters Attributes Name: Kadian Emperor Race: Kadian Title: Emperor of the Kadian Empire Location: High Citadel, Kadia Factions: Kadian Court The Kadian Emperor is the supreme ruler of the Kadian Empire. His court resides in the Stone High Citadel in the Province of Kadia, overseeing the affairs of the empire and its provinces. Background The current emperor ascended the throne after the sudden death of his father. Known for his cold pragmatism and obsession with control, his reign has been defined by both territorial expansion and increasing internal surveillance. Personality He speaks little but observes much, trusting only a small circle of advisors and military officers. docs.text: Kadian Learns quickly and ancient by lineage, the Kadians are the oldest civilization in the Empire. They see themselves as the rightful heirs of order, believing their existence is the result of the gods’ triumph over chaos. Their province is ruled by kings and built in stone, set among dry fields and fortified cities. Over centuries they have both conquered and freed other peoples, leaving a complicated legacy. Much of modern life traces back to Kadian invention: irrigation, chimneys, roads, the court system, the first legal code of laws and consequences, and the modern concept of time in the form of the sundial. docs.text: Alchemy Alchemy represents your ability to craft potent potions and putrid poisons. It relies on Intelligence, and the application of trial and error. Perks Supplements: Lvl 10, primary effects of ingredients you consume last very slightly longer. Best Bits: Lvl 20, potions and poisons you craft are 20% stronger. Herb Lore: Lvl 30, learn 2nd effect for all ingredients. Alchemist's Pouch: Lvl 40, alchemical ingredients have no weight. Stable Compounds: Lvl 50, potions and poisons you craft are 40% stronger. Herbal Mastery: Lvl 60, learn all 3 effects of all ingredients. Ampoule Band: Lvl 70, potions the player makes have no weight. Distilling Process: Lvl 80, when making a buff potion, remove negative effect. When making poison, remove positive effect. Potent Potions: Lvl 90, potions and poisons you craft are 60% stronger. Byproduct: Lvl 100, you create a duplicate potion when using an alchemy station. Transmutation: Lvl 110, you can create a potion with a single ingredient. Flux Brewing: Lvl 120, potions you make have a slight chance of to refund one ingredient. Grand Transmuter: Lvl 125, you create two identical potions when using an alchemy station.

docs.text: Alteration Alteration represents your skill in shaping the world around you to your liking. It relies on Willpower, as you literally bend reality to your will. Perks Defense Proficiency: Lvl 10, shields last slightly longer. Spell Efficiency: Lvl 20, alteration spells cost 10% less to cast. Defense Mastery: Lvl 30, shield spells are slightly more resistant. Apprentice Alteration: Lvl 40, tier 2 spells. Breaking and Entering: Lvl 50, lockpicking spells no longer make a sound. Weight of Worlds: Lvl 60, burden spells have a chance to paralyze their target. Journeyman Alteration: Lvl 70, tier 3 spells. Persistent Change: Lvl 80, alteration spells you cast last 30% longer. Spell Penetration: Lvl 90, alteration spells that affect targets ignore 30% of target magic resist. Expert Alteration: Lvl 100, tier 4 spells. Arcane Adaptation: Lvl 110, you gain a slight resistance to damage from spells. Security Breach: Lvl 120, you can open doors and containers locked by mundane locks. Master Alteration: Lvl 125, tier 5 spells.

docs.text: Axe The axe is not a weapon of finesse, it is a tool of finality. Each swing carries the weight of harvest and war alike, cleaving wood and bone in twain. There is no elegance in its arc, only intention. Usage Axes come in a couple shapes. Some work fine with one hand, while others require two hands to get full effectiveness. Perks Woodsman: Lvl 10, deal slightly more damage to plants and beasts when using axes. Scarred: Lvl 20, you take 10% less damage from axes. Bloodlust: Lvl 30, you deal 6% bonus damage for every 1% of your missing health. Jagged Edge: Lvl 40, 50% chance to apply bleed to enemies when using axes. Rending Strikes: Lvl 50, attacks with axes deplete more item health from armor. Bloodfury: Lvl 60, you deal 12% bonus damage for every 1% of your missing health. Serrated Edge: Lvl 70, bleeding applied with axes last 50% longer. Slightly Rusty: Lvl 80, 10-40% chance to poison based on axe durability. Bloodrage: Lvl 90, you deal bonus damage to injured enemies while weilding axes. Executioner's Cleave: Lvl 100, 15% chance to deal 225% damage to enemies when striking their head with an axe. Seam Ripper: Lvl 110, hitting enemy with an axe while they wear light armor ignores 50% of their armor. Reaper's Strike: Lvl 120, you gain massive bonus damage after killing an enemy with an axe. Sanguine's Fury: Lvl 125, you gain 50% of bleed damage you inflict with axes.

docs.text: Block Block is the art of discipline under pressure—the moment between chaos, and control. Shields become more than barriers; they are vows sworn in silence, stances held against storms. Usage Shields come in three sizes. Bucklers are small and light, standard shields offer solid protection, and great shields are large, heavy, and very protective. See Shield Types for details.
