Punisher: Lvl 30, deal a slight percentage of attack back to the attacker when blocking. Sundering Shield: Lvl 40, 10% chance to remove 10% weapon durability when weapon hits a shield. Retaliation: Lvl 50, gain bonus damage after parrying an attack. Focused: Lvl 60, increases the chances of time dilation triggering. Backlash: Lvl 70, chance to disarm on successful block. Subvert: Lvl 80, 20% chance to deflect arrow towards shooter on parry. Showstopper: Lvl 90, chance to briefly paralyze target on shield bash. Turtle: Lvl 100, shields holstered on back add to your armor. Offensive Bulwark: Lvl 110, bucklers have chance to paralyze. Sword Breaker: Lvl 120, 5% chance to shatter enemy weapon on parry. Aegis: Lvl 125, after parry, invulnerable to next physical hit.

docs.text: Conjuration Summon to your side spirits from beyond this world; be they bound to a weapon, animating the dead, or infused with the elements themselves. Perks Binding Concentration: Lvl 10, Summons last 10% longer. Warding Bond: Lvl 20, While summon is active, you gain 10% magic. Arcane Bond: Lvl 30, Slowly gain health when summons are nearby. Apprentice Conjuration: Lvl 40, tier 2 spells. Ethereal Strikes: Lvl 50, Attacks with summoned weapons ignore a slight amount of opponents armor. Soul Trap: Lvl 60, You have a chance of refilling a heart shard when your summoned creature is killed. Journeyman Conjuration: Lvl 70, tier 3 spells. Guardian Spirit: Lvl 80, Summoned creatures absorb a small amount of damage dealt to you. Twinned Soul: Lvl 90, Can summon two creatures or weapons at once. Expert Conjuration: Lvl 100, tier 4 spells. Persistent Summons: Lvl 110, you gain a slight resistance to damage from spells Ethereal Protection: Lvl 120, Summon a matching set of armor when summoning single piece. Event Horizon: Lvl 125, When a summon is dismissed, the portal has a chance to suck enemies within a radius into the void. Extras: Summoning: the art of producing creatures, weapons, or armor during a battle. Summoned weapons reflect damage when parrying. Summoned creatures are immune to non-silvered attacks. You can name one summon. It becomes more powerful each time you call it, up to a cap. Killing an enemy with a summoned weapon has a chance to recharge a heart shard.

docs.text: Enchanting Enchanting is the power to use magic on wordly objects, enhancing those objects power to use in battle. Perks Arcane Studies: Lvl 10, Enchant bench runes last slightly longer making enchanting easier. Recyclomancy: Lvl 20, When enchanting items you have a chance to have your heart shard just become depleted instead of being destroyed entirely. Mending Energies: Lvl 30, Can repair enchanted item 15% when replenishing enchantment with a shard. Twinned Enchantment: Lvl 40, Apply two enchantments to an item. Enchanter’s Guard: Lvl 50, Recharging a weapon mid combat triggers a time dilation with strength and duration equivalent to your enchant skill as if it were your block skill. Magical Overload: Lvl 60, After you recharge a weapon its next hit does 25 percent more damage. Mental Anchoring: Lvl 70, when enchanting attribute based enchantments they scale based on your current level of that attribute 10 to 20 percent stronger. Arcane Triplicate: Lvl 80, Apply three enchantments to an item. Triquetric Formulas: Lvl 90, If an enchantment uses three separate schools of magic it uses 40 percent less charge per hit. One Final Effort: Lvl 100, When an enchanted weapon is depleted the next hit has a chance to release an overcharged AOE effect based on player’s magic. Magic is drained when this happens. Divine Conduit: Lvl 110, If you hold two heart shards you can recharge any holstered weapons; the heart shards charge is divided amongst the number of holstered gear. Glorious Ascension: Lvl 120, A piece of armor you enchant with 2 effects has a 25% chance to gain a third effect of either absorb magic or reflect damage. Matrix of Eternity: Lvl 125, Apply a single permanent enchantment to a weapon.

docs.text: Hand To Hand Whether in tavern brawls, arena pits, or monastary gardens, you've learned to eshew weapons in favor of punches and kicks. Usage Hand to hand weapons include spiked knuckle gear and similar tools, but you can also fight bare‑handed by closing your fists and striking. Cheap Shot: Lvl 30, When starting each combat encounter with just fists you deal an extra 10 percent damage until you take damage. Scrappy: Lvl 40, Hand to hand weapons have a 10 percent chance to apply bleeding damage. Bellringer: Lvl 50, 25% chance to knock off an opponents headgear with hand to hand weapons. Defensive Maneuvers: Lvl 60, Activate time dilation more often. Soul Strike: Lvl 70, fist attacks are considered silvered. Brawlstar: Lvl 80, While fighting with only your fists you do 20 percent more damage and take 25 percent less damage. Knuckle Duster: Lvl 90, High chance to disarm when hitting opponents hands. Knockout: Lvl 100, 50 percent chance to ragdoll an enemy if you punch them in the head. Pressure Point: Lvl 110, When attacking with just your fists you ignore 30 percent of light armor. Punching Up: Lvl 120, When attacking with hand to hand weapons you ignore 30 percent of heavy armor. Perfect strikes: Lvl 125, Percentage chance to inflict Catatonic; paralyzed, silenced, and has their magic drained.

Culmination: Lvl 70, The third strike in an alternate direction deals 3x damage. Split Focus: Lvl 80, When facing multiple enemies take 25% less damage, but deal up to 10% less damage. Brawny: Lvl 90, Negate penalty from using two handed swords with one hand. Heft & Precisionn: Lvl 100, Great swords have a 10% chance to ragdoll an enemy. docs.text: Pickpocketing Pickpocketing is the art of silently lifting valuables, tools, or key items from unsuspecting targets. Whether it’s slipping a coin pouch from a distracted noble or lifting a cell key from a guard, pickpocketing requires finesse, timing, and a good exit plan. In the right hands, it's a tool for survival, sabotage, or just a little extra coin on the side. Perks Light Fingers, Lvl 10, +10% success rate on all pickpocket attempts. Deep Pockets, Lvl 20, Unlocks ability to steal items up to 25 gold. Slippery Escape, Lvl 30, Gain a temporary movement speed boost after a failed attempt. Inside Job, Lvl 40, +25% success when disguised. Hands of Fate, Lvl 50, Chance to gain a temporary buff of either speed, luck, or strength, after a successful pickpocket. Crowd Ghost, Lvl 60, Pickpocketing in crowds is 50% easier, and detection delay is doubled. Pressure Points, Lvl 70, Pickpocketing chance increases by 15% on targets wearing heavy armor or bulky clothing. Magpie’s Instinct, Lvl 80, Highlights high-value items in NPC inventories; +10% to steal rare or enchanted items. Misdirection, Lvl 90, Temporarily distracts a target, lowering their awareness for 5 seconds before the attempt. Silent Snatch, Lvl 100, Reduces the chance of a target noticing an item is missing until they try to use it or check their inventory. Spider’s Touch, Lvl 110, Pickpocketing now works during stealth takedowns, letting you steal key items mid-ambush. Cutpurse's Edge, Lvl 120, Gain a small amount of health each time you successfully pickpocket, scaling with item value. Master Thief, Lvl 125, Guaranteed success on pickpocket attempts of common items and minor magical trinkets.

Reserve Power: Lvl 90, Spells cast through staves are strengthened by your skill in their governing school. Lightning Rod: Lvl 100, Regain spell charges when hitting creatures with active spell effects. Echoes: Lvl 120, after a spell effect ends you have a 20 percent chance for a weakened version of the same spell to appear at the same location 2 seconds later. Event Horizon: Lvl 125, Staff spells track the first enemy they hit for the duration of their effect.

docs.text: Wand With a swish and a flick, simple sticks become implements of your will. Your power is precision, practiced to dazzle minds and scorch foes. Usage Wands focus your magic into projectile spells. At low skill they cast a basic projectile; at higher skill you can channel a spell of your choice for greater damage. Perks Defense: Lvl 10, 10% magic resistance while using wands. Attunement: Lvl 20, You unlock the ability to attune wands with your own spells. Pinpoint: Lvl 30, When hitting an enemy with a wand spell, there is a 10% chance to stun them. Spell Dueling: Lvl 40, 15% chance to disarm enemies when hitting them with wand spells. Breaking and Entering: Lvl 50, Wand spells now have a 20% chance to cause durability loss on enemies weapons, this percentage is doubled if the enemy is using a wand. Willthief: Lvl 60, 25% chance to immediately pacify anyone when hitting them with a wand spell. Mage Sight: Lvl 70, Time dilates when a magic projectile is coming at player, player can then deflect the projectile with a wand. Siphon: Lvl 80, When using a wand to deflect projectile spells, you absorb a percent of the magic spent to cast that spell. Paralytic : Lvl 90, 20% chance to paralyze enemy when hitting them with a wand spell. Maddening Cast: Lvl 100, 40% chance to frenzy an enemy when hitting them with a wand spell. Neutralize: Lvl 110, 50% chance to silence enemy hit with wand spell. Unforgiveable: Lvl 120, You have a 10% chance to instantly kill an enemy with a wand spell. Gatekeeper: Lvl 125, When killing an enemy with a spell cast through a wand, there is a 20% chance to completely refill your magic.

docs.text: Kadian Quick Jump Base Attributes Skill Bonuses Resistences Other Information Learns quickly. Ancient. The oldest civilization in the Empire. Thinks themselves higher than other races. Lives in dry fields. Province controlled by kings. Believes their existence is the result of the God's triumph over chaos. Lives in stone buildings. Has taken and freed other races into slavery throughout their history. Their civilization has come up with most of the modern innovations such as irrigation, chimneys, roads, the court system and the first legal code of laws and consequences, and the modern concept of time in the form of a sundial. docs.text: Farick Crane Quick Jump Background Personality Related Characters Attributes Name: Farick Crane Race: Roccan Title: Bookmaker Location: Rustfall Arena Factions: Bookmaker Farick is a charismatic and shrewd bookmaker who orchestrates the gambling scene surrounding the arena matches. His calculating mind is always assessing odds and outcomes, and his silver tongue persuades both rich and poor to bet on matches. Background Farick and Maerigrim have a secret alliance built around shared understandings by underhanded business folk. Maerigrim provides magical insights to matches, either to divine or force the outcome, and in return Farick uses his social network to stamp out any business competition for the arcanist. docs.text: Mauzara "Dragonheart" Quick Jump Background Personality Related Characters Attributes Name: Mauzara Race: Antanian Title: Red Team Trainer Location: Rustfall Arena Factions: Red Team Growing up working in the Arena, Mauzara stepped into the ring at an early age and quickly became a crowd favorite, earning the title “Dragonheart” for her unmatched skill in both offense and defense. Now retired from the Arena, she imparts her battle wisdom to the Red Team. Gruff but fair, she pushed her fighters to their limits, ensuring they are prepared for any challenge. Background While she understands the practicality of using magic, and uses several enchanted items herself, she has always been wary of spellcasters and people who rely on magic to solve their problems. Mauzara is a bit naive about how life is outside of the Arena and will occasionally ask the player questions about their life outside. docs.text: Sevryn "Shadowstep" Enakam Quick Jump Background Personality Related Characters Attributes Name: Sevryn "Shadowstep" Enakam Race: Saloen Title: Blue Team Trainer Location: Rustfall Arena Factions: Blue Team Sevryn, once an elusive assassin, now trains the Blue Team with their stealth and precision. They value strategy and cunning as much as strength, teaching their fighters to anticipate an opponents’ moves and strike at the perfect time. Beneath their stoic exterior, they care deeply for their fighters, forging unbreakable bonds with each one. Background They rarely talk about their past and talk guardedly, for a variety of reasons, but will often add cryptic and sarcastic comments in conversations with people they are comfortable with. Site Design Reference This page is the style guide for the Heartlands Codex. Keep entries concise, consistent, and easy to scan. Headers # for page title ## for primary sections ### for subsections Lists Use bullet lists for quick facts and scannable sections. Collapsible Sections Use collapsible blocks for long lore or spoilers. Click to expand history The Kadian Empire was founded in... Linking Use relative links so pages work locally and on GitHub Pages. Race: Kadian Galleries Use the gallery pattern for pages with multiple images. The gallery supports a large main image with a thumbnail strip. Example:
Notes: * Keep images relative to the current page. * Use the same image list for the main carousel and thumbnails. Infoboxes Use infoboxes for key stats and profiles so pages read consistently.
Item Stats
Weight0.0
Value0.0
Page Templates Use these templates when creating new pages. Copy one and fill it out: * NPC Template * Location Template * Item Template * Quest Template * Faction Template * Race Template Tags Tags help group related pages. Add tags in a front matter block at the very top of a page: --- tags: [example, lore, faction] --- See the Tags Index for available tags. Regenerating Indexes And Tags If you add or remove pages, run the helper script to rebuild indexes, tags, and the home page “Latest Additions”. python3 docs/tools/regenerate_indexes_and_tags.py Quick Jump Use quick jump buttons for longer pages so readers can jump to sections. Example: ## Quick Jump * [Summary](#summary) * [Appearance](#appearance) * [History](#history) Links and Paths Use pretty URLs and relative links without .md where possible. Examples: Good: ../Skills/ShortBlade/ Good: ../Gameplay/ShieldTypes/#buckler-shields Avoid: ../Skills/ShortBlade.md
